title: US Civil Rights
group: HIST-TOPIC — Overview Anchors (each links to deeper subdomains)
examples: What were some of the main goals of the Civil Rights Movement?
Can you explain the impact of the Civil Rights Act?
Who were some important leaders during this time period?

explain.say: The Civil Rights Movement fought for equal rights for African Americans.
One key event was the Montgomery Bus Boycott in 1955.
Rosa Parks was a key leader in this movement.
The Supreme Court case Brown versus Board of Education was very important.
Later legislation like the Civil Rights Act of 1964 banned discrimination.
In everyday life, this movement changed where people could go.

faq.a: Segregation meant that different racial groups were forced to live and go to school separately. It was a system of enforced separation.
asks: Why were people separated by race?

faq.q: Why was Brown versus Board so significant?
faq.a: It overturned the idea that separate schools were acceptable. The court ruled that separate educational facilities were inherently unequal.
asks: Did Brown v Board end segregation completely?
What did the Supreme Court decide in Brown v Board?

faq.q: What was the role of non-violent protest?
faq.a: Non-violent protest, like sit-ins, was a powerful tool. It showed the public the injustice without physical violence.

faq.q: Which piece of legislation was particularly important?
faq.a: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 was crucial. It outlawed discrimination based on race, color, religion, or national origin.
asks: Was the Civil Rights Act the final law?

faq.q: Were there other leaders besides Rosa Parks?
faq.a: Yes, Martin Luther King Jr. was a very important leader. He helped organize many major peaceful demonstrations.
asks: Who was Martin Luther King Jr.?
Besides Parks, who led the movement?

facts: Segregation was a system enforcing racial separation in public life.
The Montgomery Bus Boycott began in 1955.
Brown versus Board of Education ruled against 'separate but equal'.
The Civil Rights Act of 1964 banned many forms of discrimination.

quiz.say: The ruling that separate educational facilities were unequal came from:
quiz.why: This ruling directly challenged the legal basis for racial separation in schools.

wrong.0: This was a protest action, not a Supreme Court legal ruling.
wrong.1: This document dealt with freedom from slavery, which was a different historical issue.
wrong.3: This was a law that banned discrimination, but it was not the initial court ruling.

quiz.say: Which event is best known for non-violent protest against bus seating rules?
quiz.why: This boycott showed the power of organized, peaceful community action.

wrong.0: While important, the boycott specifically focused on public transportation seating.
wrong.1: This campaign focused more specifically on voting rights at the polls.
wrong.2: These rides targeted interstate bus travel, but the boycott is the key event for local bus segregation.

quiz.say: The primary goal of the legislation passed was to:
quiz.why: The legislation aimed to create federal laws ensuring equal treatment across all aspects of life.

wrong.0: The legislation focused on civil rights, not general economic support.
wrong.1: While voting rights were key, the legislation covered broader areas like employment and public accommodation.
wrong.2: Change happened through a combination of court rulings and federal acts over time.
